policy_title: Strengthen Armed Forces Covenant and Improve MOD Housing
stated: Securing a fair deal for the armed forces community, and improve recruitment, retention and resettlement, by: Strengthening the Armed Forces Covenant by placing a legal duty on the Defence Secretary and government departments to give it due regard. Improving the standard of Ministry of Defence housing, including by reviewing maintenance contracts.

source.quote: Securing a fair deal for service personnel and veterans. Secure a fair deal for the armed forces community, and improve recruitment, retention and resettlement, by: Strengthening the Armed Forces Covenant by placing a legal duty on the Defence Secretary and government departments to give it due regard. Improving the standard of Ministry of Defence housing, including by reviewing maintenance contracts.

bearing_set.reason: Improving recruitment, retention and resettlement directly affects armed forces capability and national security/defence posture, a core O5 indicator.
Improving MOD housing standards directly affects the quality and adequacy of homes available to service personnel and their families, a real housing-stock effect.
The policy is stated to improve recruitment, retention and resettlement, directly bearing on employment conditions, job security and career transitions for armed forces personnel.

The Armed Forces Covenant is explicitly an equal-treatment instrument, ensuring service personnel and veterans face no disadvantage accessing public services; placing a legal duty on government departments creates enforceable equal-treatment rights for this group.

membership_note: Three genuine bearings: the covenant's legal duty is a real equal-treatment mechanism (O9); MOD housing and fair-deal provisions are conditions of service (O4); and the recruitment/retention aims directly bear on defence capability (O5). No O1 bearing: MOD housing quality improvements do not affect house-price-to-income ratios or general affordable-housing stock indicators.
